routes.name: Skyline Loop (North Fork Quinault - Low Divide - Skyline Ridge)

trailheads.name: North Fork Quinault Trailhead

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness camping permit required year-round; reserve via Recreation.gov ($6 reservation fee plus $8/person/night, summer reservations open April 15). Permits issued per campsite/zone.
routes.highlights: A high, remote ridge traverse past Kimta Peak, Lake Beauty and Three Prune with in-your-face views of Mount Olympus above the Quinault rainforest, closed via the Low Divide and North Fork Quinault valley.
routes.hazards: Unbridged fords (Wild Rose Creek, Elip Creek, Quinault River) that can become impassable in rain, faint primitive tread requiring expert navigation between Kimta Peak and Lake Beauty, lingering snow into August, black bears.
routes.status_2026: Passable but rough as of July 2026: Stalding Creek bridge on the North Fork Quinault Trail damaged and considered closed (NPS 7/27/26), ~35 blowdowns between 11-mile camp and Low Divide, brushy tread on the Skyline side; South Shore Road washed out, so drive North Shore Road to the trailhead.

routes.name: Press Expedition Traverse (Elwha River to North Fork Quinault)

trailheads.name: Whiskey Bend Trailhead (Elwha)
North Fork Quinault Trailhead

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness camping permit via Recreation.gov ($6 reservation + $8/person/night); Elwha and North Fork Quinault valley campsites reserved per site, not high-competition quota areas.
routes.highlights: The historic 1889-90 Press Expedition line across the Olympics, following the Elwha River through Geyser Valley and Press Valley over Low Divide (3,602 ft) and down the North Fork Quinault rainforest.
routes.hazards: Required ford of the Elwha south of Chicago Camp (log crossing washed away), heavy blowdown, overgrown tread between Low Divide and Chicago Camp, black bears.
routes.status_2026: Olympic Hot Springs Road/Whiskey Bend Road remain closed to vehicles from the 2021 washout (pedestrians/bikes OK), adding ~6.3 road miles from Madison Falls to Whiskey Bend (~50 mi total); ~22 blowdowns Whiskey Bend-Elkhorn (NPS 6/14/26); Stalding Creek bridge on the North Fork Quinault Trail closed (NPS 7/27/26).

routes.name: Enchanted Valley and Anderson Pass (East Fork Quinault)

trailheads.name: Graves Creek Trailhead

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness camping permit via Recreation.gov ($6 + $8/person/night); Enchanted Valley campsites are extremely popular - reserve when the summer window opens April 15. Bear canisters required in Enchanted Valley.
routes.highlights: Rainforest river walk past Pony Bridge to the 'Valley of 10,000 Waterfalls' and its historic chalet, then a 2,500-ft climb to Anderson Pass beneath the Anderson Glacier cirque (13 mi + 5.2 mi each way per NPS).
routes.hazards: White Creek ford can be hazardous during heavy rain/snowmelt, a washed-out trail section just before the chalet, snow on Anderson Pass into July, very active black bears in the valley.
routes.status_2026: Open with a washed-out stretch of trail shortly before the Enchanted Valley chalet and ~14 blowdowns above O'Neil Creek (NPS 7/27/26); South Shore Road washed out - reach Graves Creek Road via North Shore Road.

routes.name: Grand Valley - Cameron Creek Loop (Obstruction Point)

trailheads.name: Obstruction Point Trailhead
Deer Park Trailhead

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness camping permit via Recreation.gov ($6 + $8/person/night); Grand Valley (Grand/Moose/Gladys Lakes) is a limited-quota area that books out quickly for summer.
routes.highlights: Tundra-like ridge walking on Lillian Ridge into lake-dotted Grand Valley, over 6,450-ft Grand Pass into lonely Cameron Basin country, returning via Three Forks and the high Deer Park-Obstruction Point ridge (a Gray Wolf Pass/Dose Meadows extension makes it a ~44-mi 'Grand Loop').
routes.hazards: Steep snowfields on Grand Pass into mid-July, two Cameron Creek crossings difficult in heavy rain, a 2,400-ft-in-1.6-mi descent, and a long exposed waterless ridge on the return leg.
routes.status_2026: No closures on the loop itself; Obstruction Point Road open as of 6/17/26 and Deer Park Road open as of 6/9/26 (the separate Lower Graywolf Trail washout only affects access from the Graywolf trailhead).

routes.name: North Olympic Coast: Shi Shi Beach to Rialto Beach

trailheads.name: Shi Shi Beach Trailhead (Makah Reservation)
Rialto Beach Trailhead (Mora Road)

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness permit via Recreation.gov, limited-quota reservations required for all coast camps between Point of the Arches and Yellow Banks, bear canisters mandatory. A Makah Recreation Pass (purchased in Neah Bay) additionally required to park at Shi Shi trailhead.
routes.highlights: The wildest beach walk in the Lower 48: Point of the Arches sea stacks, the Ozette River mouth, Wedding Rocks petroglyphs at Cape Alava, and Hole-in-the-Wall (NPS splits it as ~15 mi Shi Shi-Ozette plus ~20 mi Ozette-Rialto).
routes.hazards: Tide-trapped headlands with 4-6 ft tide windows that have killed hikers (carry a tide chart), a low-tide-only ford of the Ozette River, steep slick overland rope-and-ladder trails around impassable points.
routes.status_2026: Mora Road closed past Mora Campground for construction 7/8/26-10/15/26, making the Rialto Beach terminus inaccessible during that window (exit at Ozette instead, or go after mid-October); Ozette River ford passable in summer; Hoko-Ozette Road open.

routes.name: Hoh River Trail to Glacier Meadows and Blue Glacier

trailheads.name: Hoh River Trailhead (Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center)

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness camping permit via Recreation.gov ($6 + $8/person/night); Hoh River Valley campsites (Five Mile Island, Lewis Meadow, Elk Lake, Glacier Meadows) reserved per site, very high summer demand.
routes.highlights: Seventeen nearly flat miles through the mossy old-growth Hoh rainforest, then a 3,000-ft climb to Glacier Meadows and the lateral moraine overlooking Mount Olympus's crevassed Blue Glacier.
routes.hazards: A major washout with a fixed rope/ladder descent about half a mile before Glacier Meadows, two fords before Olympus Guard Station, the airy High Bridge gorge crossing, snow on the moraine into July.
routes.status_2026: Open: Upper Hoh Road open (5/5/26), the two fords before Olympus Guard Station at low flow (NPS 6/1/26), ~37 blowdowns along the valley (NPS 6/14/26), the Glacier Meadows washout ladder remains the crux.

routes.name: High Divide - Seven Lakes Basin Loop (Sol Duc)

trailheads.name: Sol Duc Trailhead (road end)

routes.permits: Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin/Mink Lake is one of Olympic NP's most competitive quota zones: reserve camps on Recreation.gov when summer permits release April 15 at 7am PT ($6 reservation + $8/person/night). Bear canisters required; park entrance fee for parking.
routes.highlights: Alpine lake basin and ridge walk with head-on views of Mount Olympus and the Blue Glacier, Heart Lake, Bogachiel Peak, and abundant bears and marmots.
routes.hazards: Snow lingers on north/east aspects of the High Divide into mid-July, and habituated black bears frequent the basin camps.
routes.status_2026: No known closures; Sol Duc Road open (3/24/26); NPS reported patchy snow on High Divide's north/east aspects in early summer 2026.

routes.name: South Coast Wilderness Trail (Third Beach to Oil City)

trailheads.name: Third Beach Trailhead (La Push Rd)
Oil City Trailhead (Hoh River mouth)

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness permit required via Recreation.gov (no trailhead self-issue anymore); south-coast camps (Scott Creek, Toleak Point, Mosquito Creek) are not in the April-15 quota lottery but summer weekends can book up. Bear canister mandatory; groups max 12.
routes.highlights: Wildest beach backpack in the Pacific Northwest's Lower 48: sea stacks at Giants Graveyard and Toleak Point, tidepools, eagles, and camps on the sand.
routes.hazards: Tide-gated headlands (Diamond Rock passable below ~2 ft, south of Scott Creek below ~4 ft), steep rope-and-ladder overland trails, fords of Goodman, Falls and Mosquito creeks that swell fast in rain.
routes.status_2026: Open, but NPS reports a major washout at Scott's Bluff (8-10 ft embankment) passable only at tides below ~1 ft; Goodman Overland route muddy/brushy; the Mora Road closure affects Rialto, not this section.

routes.name: Bailey Range Traverse
routes.difficulty: expert - multi-day off-trail travel, exposed scrambling (the Catwalk), steep snow

trailheads.name: Sol Duc Trailhead (start)
Madison Falls / Elwha (typical exit; road closed to cars beyond)

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness permit via Recreation.gov: the first night is usually inside the competitive Seven Lakes Basin/High Divide quota zone (Heart Lake), with later nights in undesignated cross-country zones; book April 15 for summer.
routes.highlights: The Olympics' classic high route from the High Divide past Mount Carrie, Cream Lake, Ferry Basin and Bear Pass, exiting via Dodwell-Rixon Pass and the Elwha Snowfinger or the Dodger Point variant (roughly 40-50 trail-plus-cross-country miles). Off-trail sections are not drawn on this map.
routes.hazards: Days of trail-less terrain with serious exposure on the Catwalk near Mount Carrie, steep snow crossings, whiteout navigation risk, very remote rescue.
routes.status_2026: Route itself open; Elwha-side exits complicated by the Olympic Hot Springs Road washout (closed to vehicles at Madison Falls, bikes allowed) plus 2023 fire damage, blowdowns, and a required ford south of Chicago Camp.

routes.name: Enchanted Valley - O'Neil Pass - LaCrosse Basin Lollipop

trailheads.name: Graves Creek Trailhead

routes.permits: The East Fork Quinault corridor is now a quota area (pilot begun 2024: max 208 users or 30 permits/night), so reserve camps on Recreation.gov starting April 15; Marmot Lake, Upper Duckabush and LaCrosse Pass-side camps are non-quota but still permit-only. Bear canisters required.
routes.highlights: Up the East Fork Quinault past the Enchanted Valley chalet, along O'Neil Pass's miles-long balcony above the Duckabush, into LaCrosse Basin (Marmot, Hart and LaCrosse lakes), returning over LaCrosse and Anderson passes - the truest ~50-miler in the Olympics.
routes.hazards: Multiple fords (White Creek, Upper Duckabush - hazardous through early summer), heavy blowdown, high-country snow into July, one of the park's densest black bear populations.
routes.status_2026: Open with obstacles: washed-out tread ~two-thirds of the way to Enchanted Valley forces a ford or steep bypass, ~14 logs between O'Neil Creek and the valley, and South Shore Quinault Road is washed out - reach Graves Creek via North Shore Road (no RVs/trailers).

routes.name: Constance Pass Traverse (Upper Dungeness to Dosewallips)

trailheads.name: Upper Dungeness Trailhead (FR 2870)
Dosewallips River Trailhead (washout parking)

routes.permits: Olympic NF camps (Camp Handy, Boulder Shelter) need no permit - just a NW Forest Pass at the trailhead; Olympic NP camps (Home Lake, Sunnybrook Meadows) require a Recreation.gov wilderness permit but are non-quota (the Lake Constance side trip IS a quota area).
routes.highlights: Crosses 5,850-ft Constance Pass and ~6,500-ft Del Monte Ridge with in-your-face views of Mount Constance, Warrior Peak and the inner Olympics, with marmots and mountain goats around Home Lake.
routes.hazards: The Dosewallips exit includes a 6.5-mile road walk/bike on the washed-out Dosewallips Road, water is scarce on Del Monte Ridge, snow holds on the pass into July.
routes.status_2026: Dosewallips Road remains closed to vehicles at the washout (pedestrian/bike only); NPS reported ~19 blowdowns between Constance Pass junction and Deception Creek in mid-2026.

routes.name: Marmot Pass - Buckhorn Wilderness (Upper Big Quilcene)

trailheads.name: Upper Big Quilcene Trailhead (#833, FR 2750)

routes.permits: No overnight permit needed in Olympic National Forest's Buckhorn Wilderness - just a NW Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass to park. Continuing past the pass to Home Lake crosses into Olympic NP and requires a Recreation.gov permit.
routes.highlights: Rain-shadow wildflower meadows and one of the Olympics' great pass viewpoints, with base camps at Shelter Rock and Camp Mystery and extensions to Buckhorn Mountain, Charlia Lakes, Buckhorn Lake, or a shuttle out via Tubal Cain Mine trail.
routes.hazards: Last reliable water is Camp Mystery (dry, exposed upper slopes in late summer); steep snowfields guard the pass in early season.
routes.status_2026: No known closures; regular WTA trip reports through 2026.

routes.name: Royal Basin / Royal Lake

trailheads.name: Upper Dungeness / Royal Creek Trailhead (FR 2870)

routes.permits: Royal Basin/Royal Lake is an Olympic NP quota area: reserve designated campsites on Recreation.gov when summer permits open April 15 ($6 + $8/person/night); bear canisters required, no fires above 3,500 ft. NW Forest Pass for the trailhead.
routes.highlights: Waterfall-fed Royal Lake and the milky-blue tarns of Upper Royal Basin beneath Mount Deception and The Needles - the driest, sunniest corner of the Olympics.
routes.hazards: Habituated camp rodents (chew-proof your gear), lingering snow in the upper basin into July, an unbridged Royal Creek crossing early season.
routes.status_2026: No known closures; NPS reported the trail snowfree to Royal Lake with problem rodents at the Royal Lake camp area in summer 2026.

routes.name: Upper Lena Lake (The Brothers Wilderness / Hamma Hamma)

trailheads.name: Lena Lake Trailhead (#810, Hamma Hamma Rd/FR 25)

routes.permits: Upper Lena Lake is an Olympic NP quota area - reserve one of ~10 designated sites on Recreation.gov (April 15 release for summer); bear canisters required. Lower Lena Lake (Olympic NF) needs no permit, just a NW Forest Pass.
routes.highlights: Subalpine cirque lake between Mount Lena and Mount Bretherton with wildflower meadows and off-trail side trips to Milk Lake and Scout Lake.
routes.hazards: The upper 3 miles are steep, rooty and rough; the Lena Creek crossing becomes hazardous during heavy rain or snowmelt.
routes.status_2026: No known closures; NPS listed the trail snowfree to Upper Lena in summer 2026 with the usual Lena Creek ford caution.

routes.name: North Fork Skokomish - Flapjack Lakes (Staircase)

trailheads.name: Staircase (overnight parking)

routes.permits: Flapjack Lakes (including Gladys Divide) is an Olympic NP quota area - reserve on Recreation.gov starting April 15; bear canisters required and park entrance fee at Staircase.
routes.highlights: Twin lakes under the Sawtooth Range with a rugged loop option over Black and White Lakes, and the same valley launches the primitive Six Ridge traverse toward Lake Sundown.
routes.hazards: The Black and White Lakes and Six Ridge primitive trails are blowdown-prone, faint, and dry in stretches.
routes.status_2026: CLOSED as of mid-2026: all Staircase backcountry trails (North Fork Skokomish, Flapjack Lakes, Black and White Lakes, Six Ridge) remain closed from the July 2025 Bear Gulch Fire; the Staircase developed area reopened July 8, 2026, but only the Staircase Rapids Loop is open - check NPS before planning.

routes.name: Queets River Trail
routes.difficulty: moderate trail, guarded by a serious river ford

trailheads.name: Queets River Trailhead (Upper Queets Road)

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness permit required via Recreation.gov (non-quota - normally available close to your date); bear canisters required. America the Beautiful pass for parking.
routes.highlights: The loneliest of the big west-side rainforest valleys - huge Sitka spruce, big Roosevelt elk herds, and gravel-bar camps to Spruce Bottom and Bob Creek with near-guaranteed solitude.
routes.hazards: The mandatory Queets River ford at the trailhead is safe only at low flows (NPS advises under ~800 cfs; can rise to impassable within hours of rain).
routes.status_2026: Open - Upper Queets Road open (11/13/25); NPS reports ~29 blowdowns between the ford and Bob Creek, a ~200-yard washout 0.3 mi west of Bob Creek (river bypass available), faint tread beyond Bob Creek.

routes.name: Bogachiel River Trail (rainforest valley)
routes.difficulty: moderate (mud, brush and creek crossings rather than climbing)

trailheads.name: Bogachiel River Trailhead (Undi Road)

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness permit via Recreation.gov for camps inside the park (non-quota, normally easy to get); NW Forest Pass for the trailhead. Bear canisters required in the park.
routes.highlights: The 'un-loved Hoh' - an empty temperate-rainforest valley with camps at Bogachiel Camp, Flapjack, Fifteenmile and Hyak, and a 24.4-mile point-to-point option exiting at Sol Duc (a Pacific Northwest Trail stage).
routes.hazards: Deep mud and brushy tread much of the year, numerous creek crossings that become impassable in high water, faint route-finding above Fifteenmile.
routes.status_2026: Open with damage: NPS reports a washout with a steep exposed bypass before (Bogachiel) Mosquito Creek, most Bogachiel Camp sites eroded into the river, and another washout between Flapjack and Fifteenmile.

routes.name: Dodger Point via Elwha and Long Ridge

trailheads.name: Madison Falls Trailhead (Olympic Hot Springs Rd closure point)

routes.permits: Olympic NP wilderness permit via Recreation.gov (Elwha-area camps are non-quota and usually available); park entrance fee at the Elwha entrance. The 39-mile figure includes the closed-road approach from Madison Falls (many bike it to Whiskey Bend).
routes.highlights: A historic 1933 fire lookout on a 5,753-ft meadow summit with front-row views of Mount Olympus and the Bailey Range, reached through the recovering Elwha valley.
routes.hazards: The road washout adds many flat miles each way, the Elwha corridor has standing fire-killed snags and blowdowns from the 2023 fires, snow holds on Dodger Point into July.
routes.status_2026: Olympic Hot Springs Road remains closed to vehicles at Madison Falls (pedestrians/bikes OK); NPS reports blowdowns and fire-hazard trees on the Elwha River Trail; Long Ridge Trail snowfree in summer 2026.

routes.name: Colonel Bob Peak (Pete's Creek route)

trailheads.name: Pete's Creek Trailhead (FR 2204)

routes.permits: No overnight permit needed in Olympic National Forest's Colonel Bob Wilderness - just a NW Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass at the trailhead.
routes.highlights: A 4,492-ft rocky summit rising almost from sea level with a panorama over Lake Quinault, the rainforest valley and (on clear days) the Pacific, with dispersed camps at Moonshine Flats.
routes.hazards: Steep, rocky final half-mile, boggy campsites in the wet season, snow on the upper mountain into early July, hot exposed upper slopes in summer.
routes.status_2026: No known closures on the Pete's Creek approach; note the Quinault South Shore Road washout when planning the alternative Trail #851 approach from Lake Quinault.

routes.name: West Coast Trail
routes.typical_days: 5-7 (4 days is a very fast itinerary)

trailheads.name: Pachena Bay Trailhead (near Bamfield)
Gordon River Trailhead (Port Renfrew)

routes.permits: All overnight hikers must reserve through Parks Canada at reservation.pc.gc.ca; fully reservable for the May 1-Sep 30 season, no standby. 2026 cost is $208.50 CAD/person per trip (permit + mandatory orientation), plus reservation fee (~$12) and two boat crossings (~$28 each, Gordon River and Nitinaht Narrows).
routes.highlights: Legendary 75 km shipwreck-coast route in Pacific Rim National Park Reserve with ladders, cable cars, sea stacks, Tsusiat Falls, tide-shelf walking and the Nitinaht Narrows crab shack.
routes.hazards: Over 100 ladder systems, cable cars, deep mud, tide-dependent beach sections and surge channels, fast river crossings, and black bears, wolves and cougars.
routes.status_2026: Open for 2026 season; Carmanah Point and Pachena Point light stations closed to the public; temporary fire ban in effect as of July 16, 2026.

routes.name: North Coast Trail + Cape Scott Trail

trailheads.name: Shushartie Bay Trailhead (water-taxi access only)
Cape Scott Trailhead parking lot (San Josef, 64 km west of Port Hardy)

routes.permits: No reservations; BC Parks backcountry camping fee (~$10 CAD/adult/night) via self-registration at the trailhead or BC Parks online backcountry registration. Water taxi from Port Hardy to Shushartie Bay and the trailhead road shuttle must be booked in advance.
routes.highlights: Wild, nearly empty north-tip coastline: 43.1 km North Coast Trail to Nissen Bight plus 15.4 km Cape Scott Trail past Nels Bight, with side trips to the Cape Scott lighthouse and San Josef Bay.
routes.hazards: Deep mud, two cable-car crossings with steep ladders, rope-assisted headlands, beach sections impassable at high tide, limited water sources, bears plus an active wolf advisory.
routes.status_2026: No known closures; wolf advisory in effect for Cape Scott Provincial Park; active logging trucks on the gravel access road.

routes.name: Juan de Fuca Marine Trail

trailheads.name: China Beach / Juan de Fuca East Trailhead
Botanical Beach Trailhead (Port Renfrew)

routes.permits: Backcountry permit required: $10 CAD/adult/night, purchased up to two weeks in advance at camping.bcparks.ca; campsites first-come first-served. Mid-trail access at Sombrio Beach and Parkinson Creek.
routes.highlights: 47 km of rugged surf-swept coastline a short drive from Victoria, linking Mystic Beach, Bear Beach, Sombrio Beach and the world-class tide pools of Botanical Beach.
routes.hazards: Beach sections impassable at high tide, notorious deep mud, slippery roots and boardwalks, difficult creek crossings, rogue waves, bear and cougar habitat.
routes.status_2026: Fully reopened July 1, 2026 after winter 2024-25 storm damage closed most of the trail for over a year; expect newly rebuilt bridges, boardwalks and campsites.

routes.name: Nootka Trail (Nootka Island)

trailheads.name: Louie Bay / Starfish Lagoon (floatplane drop)
Yuquot (Friendly Cove)

routes.permits: No park reservation system; hikers pay a Mowachaht/Muchalaht First Nation trail fee (~$50-75 CAD/adult plus small landing fee, via explorenootka.com, Gold River marina office, or cash at Yuquot). Floatplane (Air Nootka), water taxi, or MV Uchuck III pickup must be booked well in advance.
routes.highlights: Remote beach-walking route (~75% shoreline) past Calvin Falls, sea-otter rafts and shipwreck remains, finishing at the historic Mowachaht/Muchalaht village and lighthouse at Yuquot (Friendly Cove).
routes.hazards: Tide-dependent headland roundings, rope-assisted steep sections, three major creek/river fords, slippery shelf rock, habituated wolves and black bears.
routes.status_2026: No known closures.

routes.name: Hesquiat Peninsula Trail (Escalante Point to Boat Basin)

trailheads.name: Escalante Point (water-taxi landing)
Boat Basin, Hesquiat Harbour (floatplane/water-taxi pickup)

routes.permits: No BC Parks fee or registration in this undeveloped wilderness park; ask permission from the Hesquiaht First Nation before crossing reserve lands en route. Water-taxi drop-off and floatplane/boat pickup must be arranged well in advance.
routes.highlights: One of the least-trodden coastal expeditions on Vancouver Island - 50 km of almost continuous shoreline around the peninsula dividing Nootka and Clayoquot Sounds, past Estevan Point lighthouse and Cougar Annie's Garden.
routes.hazards: Largely trail-less rock-shelf and beach travel with deep surge channels, tide-dependent river mouths, scarce summer fresh water, wolves/bears/cougars, total self-sufficiency required.
routes.status_2026: No known closures.

routes.name: Della Falls Trail (+ Love Lake side trip)
routes.typical_days: 2-3 (plus boat access day each way if paddling)
routes.difficulty: moderate (hard with Love Lake side trip)

trailheads.name: Della Falls trailhead / ferry landing, west end of Great Central Lake (boat/floatplane access only)

routes.permits: No BC Parks camping fee or permit in the Della Falls corridor of Strathcona Park. Budget for the commercial water taxi (~$185-210 CAD/person return, daily May 15-Sep 15) or a 35 km paddle up Great Central Lake, plus paid parking at Ark Resort.
routes.highlights: Old rail-grade valley walk to the base of 440 m Della Falls, one of Canada's highest waterfalls, with the steep Love Lake spur giving a full-height view of the falls.
routes.hazards: Boat-only access (weather can delay pickup), a narrow bridge over the Drinkwater River whose handrails are removed each winter, black bears, lingering snow on the Love Lake spur into July.
routes.status_2026: No closure advisories on BC Parks as of Aug 2026; year-round ban on open fires outside provided steel rings.

routes.name: Bedwell Lakes Trail (+ Cream Lake extension)
routes.typical_days: 2-3 (3 with the ~10 km round-trip to Cream Lake)
routes.difficulty: moderate to Bedwell Lake; challenging beyond to Cream Lake

trailheads.name: Bedwell Lake trailhead, end of Jim Mitchell Lake Road (high-clearance recommended)

routes.permits: Backcountry camping permit required at Baby Bedwell and Bedwell Lake tent pads: $10 CAD/adult per night June 15-Sep 30, purchased through BC Parks' online backcountry registration (non-competitive, no quota).
routes.highlights: Fast, well-engineered access (stairs and ladders) to subalpine lakes under Mount Tom Taylor and Big Interior Mountain, with a rougher route on to turquoise Cream Lake below Mount Septimus.
routes.hazards: Steep ladder/stair sections, rough 4WD access road, bears, unmarked rocky terrain with lingering snow on the Cream Lake extension.
routes.status_2026: No closure advisories on BC Parks as of Aug 2026; park-wide campfire ban outside provided rings.

routes.name: Elk River Trail to Landslide Lake

trailheads.name: Elk River trailhead, Highway 28 near Drum Lakes

routes.permits: Backcountry camping permit required at the two designated camps (Butterwort Creek ~6 km and Gravel Bar ~9 km): $10 CAD/adult per night June 15-Sep 30 via BC Parks' online registration; camping prohibited at Landslide Lake itself.
routes.highlights: A gentle river-valley walk beneath Elkhorn and Kings Peak ending at Landslide Lake, a dramatic tarn under the sheer face of Mount Colonel Foster created by a 1946 earthquake-triggered landslide.
routes.hazards: Creek crossings and rougher, steeper tread above the Gravel Bar camp, heavy summer use, active bear country.
routes.status_2026: No closure advisories on BC Parks as of Aug 2026; year-round campfire prohibition in the backcountry.

routes.name: Forbidden Plateau: Circlet Lake & Mount Albert Edward
routes.difficulty: challenging (easy to Circlet Lake; exposed alpine route above)

trailheads.name: Paradise Meadows trailhead (Raven Lodge, Mount Washington)

routes.permits: Backcountry camping permit required at Lake Helen Mackenzie, Kwai Lake and Circlet Lake campgrounds: $10 CAD/adult per night June 15-Sep 30, bought through BC Parks' online backcountry registration (Circlet has ~60 pads; no competitive quota).
routes.highlights: Boardwalk meadows and lake-dotted plateau leading to a broad ridge walk up 2,093 m Mount Albert Edward, one of Vancouver Island's most accessible big summits.
routes.hazards: The summit route above Circlet Lake is an unmarked alpine ridge with sudden weather, whiteout navigation risk, snowfields into mid-July, no water high up.
routes.status_2026: No closure advisories on BC Parks as of Aug 2026; campfires prohibited.

routes.name: Augerpoint Traverse
routes.difficulty: very challenging - mostly unmarked alpine route

trailheads.name: Paradise Meadows trailhead (Raven Lodge, Mount Washington) - east end
Jack's Trail (Augerpoint) trailhead, Buttle Lake Parkway - west end

routes.permits: Only the Forbidden Plateau end has fee campgrounds ($10 CAD/adult/night June 15-Sep 30 via BC Parks online registration); past Circlet Lake the traverse is free wilderness camping with no permit.
routes.highlights: A high alpine crossing of Strathcona Park over Mount Albert Edward, Ruth Masters Lake and Augerpoint Mountain, descending 1,500+ m on Jack's Trail to Buttle Lake.
routes.hazards: Unmarked route with scrambling, scarce water on ridges, serious weather exposure, and a shuttle logistics problem between distant trailheads.
routes.status_2026: No closure advisories on BC Parks as of Aug 2026; campfires prohibited park-wide.

routes.name: Flower Ridge Trail
routes.difficulty: challenging (1,200 m of climbing in the first ~6 km)

trailheads.name: Flower Ridge trailhead, Buttle Lake Parkway (~26 km south of Highway 28)

routes.permits: No fees or permits - free wilderness camping outside Strathcona's fee-collection core areas; no campfires anywhere in the backcountry.
routes.highlights: A relentless climb rewarded by kilometres of open heather-and-wildflower ridge rambling with views over Buttle Lake, Mount Septimus and toward Cream Lake.
routes.hazards: Very little water on the ridge in summer (carry capacity for dry camps) and a steep, rooty descent.
routes.status_2026: No closure advisories on BC Parks as of Aug 2026.

routes.name: Marble Meadows
routes.typical_days: 2-4 (extra days for Limestone Cap or Mount McBride)

trailheads.name: Phillips Creek Marine Campsite, west shore of Buttle Lake (boat/canoe from Augerpoint or Karst Creek day-use areas)

routes.permits: No fees or permits - free wilderness camping (Phillips Creek marine site and alpine tarns); you must arrange your own boat or canoe across Buttle Lake.
routes.highlights: A 1,250 m climb to rolling limestone alpine meadows full of karst formations, tarns and wildflowers, with the Wheaton Hut and access toward Mount McBride and the Golden Hinde massif.
routes.hazards: Afternoon winds can make the Buttle Lake crossing dangerous for canoes; karst sinkholes and lingering snow demand careful travel.
routes.status_2026: No closure advisories as of Aug 2026; standing advisory about Buttle Lake boat launch hazards - check before towing a boat.

routes.name: Tatchu Peninsula (Tatchu Trail)
routes.typical_days: 4-5 (2-4 for the 28 km out-and-back from Rugged Point)

trailheads.name: Rugged Point Marine Provincial Park (water taxi from Fair Harbour, or floatplane)
Yellow Bluff Bay / Port Eliza end (water taxi from Tahsis or Zeballos)

routes.permits: No permits or trail fees; the real cost is logistics - water taxi or floatplane at each end runs several hundred dollars per person. Crosses Ehattesaht and Ka:'yu:'k't'h'/Che:k:tles7et'h' territory; no access fee currently charged.
routes.highlights: A wild, empty west-coast shoreline of sand beaches, sculpted sandstone, sea otters and tide pools between Kyuquot Sound and Esperanza Inlet - solitude the West Coast Trail can't offer.
routes.hazards: Tide-dependent headlands and surge channels, crumbling cliff bypasses (one fixed-rope descent), no marked trail or facilities beyond Rugged Point, wolves/bears.
routes.status_2026: No BC Parks advisories for Rugged Point Marine Park as of Aug 2026; coastal campfire bans in effect since mid-July 2026.

routes.name: Wild Side Trail (Flores Island)

trailheads.name: Ahousaht (Marktosis) village trailhead, Flores Island - ~30 min water taxi from Tofino
Cow Bay Beach (trail end, below Mount Flores)

routes.permits: Ahousaht Stewardship Fee of $15 CAD/person/day, payable online via the Maaqutusiis Hahoulthee Stewardship Society, at their Tofino office, or at the Ahous Fuel Stop; no BC Parks fee for the three designated camps.
routes.highlights: White-sand beaches, ancient cedar boardwalk, and gray whales feeding off Cow Bay, all in Ahousaht territory on the 'wild side' of Clayoquot Sound.
routes.hazards: Habituated wolves (active BC Parks advisory - cache all food), tide-dependent beach sections, slippery or degraded boardwalk.
routes.status_2026: BC Parks advisories as of Aug 2026: increased wolf activity (standing) and a campfire ban since July 16, 2026.

routes.name: Kludahk Trail (San Juan Ridge)
routes.difficulty: moderate (rolling subalpine ridge; route-finding and logging-road logistics)

trailheads.name: East trailhead near Jordan River (via West Jordan Main logging roads)
West trailhead toward Port Renfrew (Rosemond Lake access)

routes.permits: The trail is free and open to the public; the string of huts along it belongs to the Kludahk Outdoors Club and is members-only, so non-members must tent and carry full camping gear.
routes.highlights: A hut-dotted subalpine ridge walk above the Juan de Fuca coast through old-growth cedar, bogs, small lakes and meadows - an alpine-feeling trip within two hours of Victoria.
routes.hazards: Snow buries the ridge roughly November-June, access is via active logging roads that can be gated, sections are lightly marked with no cell coverage.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (not a BC Parks trail); confirm logging-road gate status and fire-season access restrictions with the Kludahk Outdoors Club.

routes.name: Alberni Inlet Trail

trailheads.name: Ship Creek Road trailhead, Port Alberni (north end)
China Creek Marina & Campground (mid-point road access)

routes.permits: No permits or fees; Stages 1-2 are managed by the Alberni-Clayoquot Regional District across private managed forest land, so users must stay on the trail.
routes.highlights: Bluff-top viewpoints over the fjord-like Alberni Inlet, bridged creeks and small waterfalls, and a rustic backcountry camp at 134-Mile Creek on old rail grade.
routes.hazards: Active logging surrounds the corridor (roads subject to closure), creek crossings run high after rain, legal camping limited to the one designated site.
routes.status_2026: Stages 1 and 2 (Port Alberni to Franklin River) open; the Stage 3 southern extension awaits a land-use agreement, and adjacent private roads may close during high fire danger.

routes.name: Stein Valley Traverse (Blowdown Pass to Lytton)
routes.typical_days: 4-5 (Blowdown start); 6-8 for full Lizzie Lake variant (~97 km)

trailheads.name: Blowdown Pass Trailhead (Blowdown Creek FSR off Duffey Lake Rd)
Stein Valley Trailhead (near Lytton, via Lytton reaction ferry)

routes.permits: No fees or reservations; user-maintained wilderness co-managed by BC Parks and the Lytton First Nation, first-come campsites. Campfires prohibited year-round; the Lytton ferry typically closes late May to early July for high water.
routes.highlights: BC's classic wilderness traverse: Nlaka'pamux pictographs and cultural sites along a wild undammed river valley, cable crossings, and the alpine of Blowdown Pass and the Stein divide.
routes.hazards: Remote terrain far from help with grizzly/black bears, fire-killed danger trees, landslide and rockfall zones from the 2023 burn, rough deadfall-strewn trail, rattlesnakes in the dry lower valley.
routes.status_2026: EFFECTIVELY CLOSED for thru-hiking (BC Parks advisory, June 2026): the 2023 Stein Mountain wildfire left large sections impassable - travel beyond Earls Camp from the Lytton side impossible (landslides, rockfall, hazard trees), the suspension bridge 12 km from the Lytton trailhead damaged and closed, the Cottonwood cable car removed. Limited access from Lizzie Lake and Blowdown Pass for experienced parties only. The active Ainslie Creek fire (2026) is also burning nearby.

routes.name: Garibaldi Traverse: Cheakamus Lake to Rubble Creek via Panorama Ridge and Black Tusk

trailheads.name: Cheakamus Lake Trailhead (end of Cheakamus Lake Rd, Whistler)
Rubble Creek Trailhead (Garibaldi Lake parking, Hwy 99)

routes.permits: BC Parks backcountry camping reservations required year-round for all camps (Cheakamus Lake, Helm Creek, Garibaldi Lake, Taylor Meadows) via camping.bcparks.ca; from May 15, 2026 fees are $25 CAD/adult/night + $5/youth plus a $20 flat non-resident surcharge. Day-use passes (June 12-Oct 12) not needed with proof of overnight reservation.
routes.highlights: The signature Garibaldi high country in one line: Cheakamus River old-growth, Helm Creek meadows, Cinder Flats below Black Tusk, and the famous Panorama Ridge view over turquoise Garibaldi Lake (~25 km point-to-point, ~37 km with Panorama Ridge and Black Tusk side trips).
routes.hazards: Snow lingers on Panorama Ridge and Black Tusk into mid-July, the Black Tusk chimney is a loose exposed scramble, bears frequent the meadows, and stopping is prohibited in the Barrier civil defence zone on the Rubble Creek descent.
routes.status_2026: Open; day-use passes required at Rubble Creek and Cheakamus trailheads June 12-Oct 12 (overnight reservation exempts you), high-water detour at Garibaldi Lake campground (July 2026 advisory), campfire ban since July 16, 2026.

routes.name: Elfin Lakes to Mamquam Lake (Diamond Head, Garibaldi Park)

trailheads.name: Diamond Head (Elfin Lakes) Trailhead, Garibaldi Park Rd, Squamish

routes.permits: BC Parks reservations required year-round for Elfin Lakes and Rampart Ponds via camping.bcparks.ca; from May 15, 2026 fees $25 CAD/adult/night + $20 flat non-resident surcharge. Day-use passes at Diamond Head Fri-Mon June 12-Oct 12; overnight holders exempt.
routes.highlights: Volcanic scenery unique in the corridor - the Gargoyles, Opal Cone lava flows and Ring Creek, ending at remote Mamquam Lake beneath Mamquam Mountain's glaciers.
routes.hazards: Exposed volcanic terrain with rapid weather changes, lingering early-season snow, bears, and a washed-out bridge at Zig Zag Creek that is formally closed.
routes.status_2026: PARTIALLY CLOSED: BC Parks advisory (since July 2025) - trail washed out at Zig Zag Creek ~9 km beyond Elfin Lakes; Rampart Ponds and everything beyond, including Mamquam Lake, closed until further notice with no alternate route. Elfin Lakes, Opal Cone and the Gargoyles remain open (~22-30 km trip until repaired).

routes.name: Howe Sound Crest Trail (Cypress Bowl to Porteau Cove)

trailheads.name: Cypress Mountain (Cypress Bowl) HSCT South Trailhead
Howe Sound Crest Trail Parking Area, Hwy 99 near Porteau Cove

routes.permits: No permits, fees or reservations - backcountry camping in Cypress Provincial Park is free and first-come at designated sites (Magnesia Meadows, Brunswick Lake, Deeks Lake), with small emergency shelters at Magnesia Meadows and Brunswick Lake.
routes.highlights: A rollercoaster ridgeline past St. Mark's Summit, Unnecessary Mountain and the iconic Lions, with nonstop views over Howe Sound fjord.
routes.hazards: Technical exposed sections with fixed ropes and scrambling around the West Lion and James/David peaks where a fall could be fatal, plus very scarce water between Cypress and Magnesia Meadows.
routes.status_2026: No known trail closures; Cypress Bowl Road paving work (June 30-Oct 31, 2026) may affect access to the south trailhead; campfire ban since July 16, 2026.

routes.name: Tenquille-Owl Lakes Traverse (Pemberton)

trailheads.name: Owl Lake Trailhead (Owl Creek FSR)
Tenquille Lake Branch 12 Trailhead (Hurley FSR Branch 12)

routes.permits: No permits, fees or reservations - Crown land / recreation sites managed with the Pemberton Wildlife Association; the Tenquille Lake cabin is first-come by donation. Both access roads require high-clearance 4WD.
routes.highlights: A quiet alpine meadow-and-tarn traverse between Owl Lake and Tenquille Lake with big Pemberton Valley views and far fewer people than Garibaldi (~23 km trailhead-to-trailhead; ~32 km from lower road starts).
routes.hazards: Faint tread with real routefinding through talus and seasonal snow, grizzly habitat, rough 4WD-only access roads at both ends.
routes.status_2026: No known closures as of mid-2026, but the Twin Two Creek fire (out of control, 2026) is burning east of Pemberton - check status and smoke before driving.

routes.name: Sunshine Coast Trail: Sarah Point to Powell River (hut-to-hut)

trailheads.name: Sarah Point Trailhead, Desolation Sound (water taxi or 4x4 from Lund)
Shingle Mill / Powell Lake bridge trailhead, Powell River

routes.permits: Completely free - no permits, fees or reservations; the huts on this section (Manzanita, Rieveley's Pond, Shangri-La) are first-come first-served, so carry a tent as backup. Book the Lund-Sarah Point water taxi in advance.
routes.highlights: Canada's longest free hut-to-hut trail: this northernmost section links Desolation Sound ocean bluffs, old-growth pockets and the Scout Mountain viewpoint over Powell Lake, finishing at a pub (typical 4-day split: 16 + 17.4 + 9.7 + 7.1 km).
routes.hazards: Water sources can dry up on the bluffs in late summer, hut space never guaranteed, active logging roads and cutblocks; across Georgia Strait from the Sea-to-Sky proper - two ferries or a water taxi to reach.
routes.status_2026: No known closures as of mid-2026; active logging occasionally forces short reroutes - check sunshinecoasttrail.com before you go.

routes.name: Musical Bumps - Russet Lake (Kees and Claire Hut) - Singing Pass loop

trailheads.name: Singing Pass Trailhead, Whistler Village
Whistler Village Gondola base (lift access to Musical Bumps)

routes.permits: Camping at Russet Lake requires a year-round BC Parks backcountry reservation ($25 CAD/adult/night + $6/pad transaction fee, 3-month rolling window); the Kees and Claire Hut books separately via Spearhead Huts Society (~$50/person/night). Whistler Blackcomb lift ticket for the Musical Bumps start.
routes.highlights: Ridgeline alpine walking over Flute and Oboe summits to a modern 38-person hut below Fissile Peak, with Cowboy Ridge and Overlord Glacier viewpoints as extensions.
routes.hazards: Exposed alpine ridges with fast-changing weather, late-season snow patches, no water between Oboe Summit and Russet Lake.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); regional smoke possible from the Twin Two Creek and Pear Lake fires.

routes.name: Garibaldi Lake / Taylor Meadows base camp (Panorama Ridge + Black Tusk)
routes.difficulty: moderate (long mileage; side trips add scree)

trailheads.name: Rubble Creek Trailhead

routes.permits: BC Parks backcountry reservation mandatory year-round at Garibaldi Lake and Taylor Meadows campgrounds ($25 CAD/adult/night + $6/pad fee, 3-month rolling window). Day-use vehicle pass at Rubble Creek Fri-Mon June 12-Oct 12, 2026; backcountry reservation holders exempt.
routes.highlights: Turquoise 300-m-deep lake base camp with the two classic day objectives - Panorama Ridge (2,133 m) and the Black Tusk shoulder - without the traverse logistics.
routes.hazards: Black bears frequent the campgrounds, side trips hold snow into July, the Black Tusk chimney is loose class-3+ rock.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); day-pass system in effect; regional wildfire smoke possible.

routes.name: Wedgemount Lake (Garibaldi Provincial Park)
routes.difficulty: hard (1,200 m in 7 km, boulder slope finish)

trailheads.name: Wedgemount Lake Trailhead (end of Wedge Creek FSR branch)

routes.permits: BC Parks backcountry reservation required year-round for the 20 tent pads; $25 CAD/adult/night + $6/pad fee on the 3-month rolling window. The small Wedgemount hut is emergency shelter only.
routes.highlights: Glacier-fed lake at 1,900 m beneath Wedge Mountain and Armchair Glacier, with day scrambles toward the Wedgemount Glacier toe.
routes.hazards: Very steep grade, slippery when wet, late-lingering snow on the upper boulder field, cold alpine nights.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); regional wildfire smoke possible.

routes.name: Brew Lake and Brew Hut via Roe Creek

trailheads.name: Roe-Brew Trail start, Roe Creek FSR (2WD parking at km 5.9 bridge)

routes.permits: No permits or fees; Brew Hut (sleeps ~10-12) is a free first-come VOC hut - donations welcomed - and camping at Brew Lake is unrestricted crown land.
routes.highlights: Quiet heather-and-tarn alpine around Brew Lake with a character-filled summit-ridge hut and an easy walk-up of Mount Brew.
routes.hazards: The final section above Brew Lake is unmarked off-trail terrain where whiteouts are common; the deactivated Roe Creek road is deteriorating.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); regional wildfire smoke possible.

routes.name: Brandywine Meadows and Brandywine Mountain overnight
routes.difficulty: moderate to meadows; summit day adds ~900 m

trailheads.name: Brandywine Meadows lower trailhead, Brandywine FSR (2WD)

routes.permits: No permits, fees or reservations - free backcountry camping in the meadows (no facilities); outside any provincial park on a BC rec-site tenure.
routes.highlights: Huge wildflower meadows at 1,500 m under Brandywine Mountain, whose 2,213 m summit is one of the best effort-to-view scrambles in the corridor.
routes.hazards: Steep, rooty, often muddy trail, no toilets or food caches (bear country), rough 4WD-only upper road.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); regional wildfire smoke possible.

routes.name: Semaphore Lakes base camp (Railroad Pass, Hurley FSR)
routes.difficulty: easy-moderate walk in; scrambles from camp

trailheads.name: Semaphore Lakes Trailhead, Hurley River FSR km 14.3 (Railroad Pass)

routes.permits: No permits or reservations - free first-come camping at designated areas by each of the three lakes (BC recreation site); toilets and food caches provided, no campfires.
routes.highlights: Alpine tarns beneath Locomotive and Face Mountains reached in barely an hour - one of the easiest true-alpine base camps in the region.
routes.hazards: Grizzly and black bear country with fierce early-July bugs; the Hurley FSR is a rough gravel road.
routes.status_2026: Trail open, but the Hurley FSR is currently a designated evacuation route for the Bonanza Creek fire near Gold Bridge - check SLRD updates and expect smoke (early Aug 2026).

routes.name: Train Glacier Traverse (Face - Caboose - Tender - Locomotive)
routes.difficulty: very hard - off-trail, class 2-3 scrambling, glacier-margin travel

trailheads.name: Semaphore Lakes Trailhead, Hurley River FSR km 14.3 (Railroad Pass)

routes.permits: No permits or fees; camp free at Semaphore Lakes and do the five-summit circumnavigation of the Train Glacier as a big day from camp. Off-trail sections are not drawn on this map.
routes.highlights: Five summits ringing the crevassed Train Glacier with nonstop views over the Pemberton Icefield - a blog-classic mountaineer's backpack.
routes.hazards: Serious routefinding, rockfall (helmets recommended), a committing glacier-outflow creek crossing, a loose disorienting descent off Locomotive.
routes.status_2026: Route open; Hurley FSR currently doubles as a Bonanza Creek fire evacuation route - verify SLRD status and smoke before committing (early Aug 2026).

routes.name: Joffre Lakes (Pipi7iyekw) - Upper Lake overnight

trailheads.name: Joffre Lakes Trailhead, Hwy 99 (Duffey Lake Rd)

routes.permits: Overnight camping viable in 2026: Upper Joffre Lake campground reservations (3-month rolling window) for arrivals from June 15, $25 CAD/adult/night + $6/pad fee; campers exempt from the free day-use pass required May 11-Oct 25.
routes.highlights: Three glacier-blue lakes under Matier Glacier with tent pads steps from the upper lake - one of BC's most photogenic legal backcountry camps.
routes.hazards: Heavy crowds, icefall-fed cold water, rockfall/serac hazard toward the Matier moraines.
routes.status_2026: Open with day-pass system; park fully CLOSED June 20-27 and Sept 8-30, 2026 for First Nations cultural use; Twin Two Creek fire burns ~20 km south - no Hwy 99 closure as of early Aug 2026 but expect smoke.

routes.name: Marriott Basin / Wendy Thompson Hut (with Rohr Lake option)

trailheads.name: Marriott Basin parking, Hwy 99 near Cayoosh Creek

routes.permits: The ACC-Whistler Wendy Thompson Hut (sleeps 16) must be reserved and prepaid online - $25 CAD/person/night ($20 ACC members); tenting in the meadows away from the hut is free and permit-less on crown land.
routes.highlights: A gothic-arch hut at treeline in a lake-dotted granite basin, with Marriott Lake, Aspen Peak col, and adjacent Rohr Lake as uncrowded objectives.
routes.hazards: Scattered boulder fields between hut and upper basin, thin signage, early-summer snow.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); smoke possible from the Twin Two Creek fire to the south.

routes.name: Cerise Creek / Keith's Hut (Anniversary Glacier)

trailheads.name: Cerise Creek summer trailhead pullout, Hwy 99 (Duffey Lake Rd)

routes.permits: First-come, first-served hut (sleeps 14) in Nlhaxten/Cerise Creek Conservancy - no booking system; donations with a suggested minimum of $25 CAD/person/night for groups. Tenting near the hut is free.
routes.highlights: Treeline hut at 1,650 m under Joffre Peak's north faces and the Anniversary Glacier, a mountaineering hub for Mount Matier.
routes.hazards: The marked route crosses the 2019 Joffre Peak landslide path where a third slide is considered possible - cross quickly; swollen creeks and glaciated terrain above.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); the sanctioned reroute around the slide path remains in effect; Duffey corridor smoke possible.

routes.name: Phelix Creek / Brian Waddington Hut at Long Lake

trailheads.name: Phelix Creek FSR 4WD road end (summer trailhead)

routes.permits: VOC hut (sleeps ~25) with no reservation system - register your trip on the VOC wiki and donate $10 CAD/person/night if not a member; free tent sites line Long Lake.
routes.highlights: Lakeside hut beneath the granite spires of Mount Gandalf, Aragorn and Shadowfax, with easy scrambles and swimming from camp.
routes.hazards: Grizzly feeding habitat - the VOC strongly discourages visits Aug 15-Oct 15 - and the spur road needs high clearance.
routes.season: July to mid-August is prime (voluntary grizzly closure Aug 15-Oct 15)
routes.status_2026: No known fire closures (early Aug 2026), but the voluntary grizzly closure starts Aug 15; smoke possible.

routes.name: Watersprite Lake (BCMC hut and tent platforms)

trailheads.name: Watersprite Lake Trailhead gate near Skookum Dam (Mamquam FSR km 13.2 turnoff)

routes.permits: Camping is on 14 BCMC tent platforms plus 6 tent sites at $25 CAD/platform/night (2026), reservable max 60 days ahead at recsites.bcmc.ca; the 8-person hut books as a whole ($300/night). No dogs.
routes.highlights: Turquoise cirque lake under Dreadnought and Martin Peaks with the corridor's best-appointed club infrastructure close to Squamish.
routes.hazards: Rough FSR access (high clearance helps), exposed talus near the lake outlet, platforms book out almost instantly for summer weekends.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); regional wildfire smoke possible.

routes.name: Lake Lovely Water (Tantalus Provincial Park)
routes.difficulty: hard (1,135 m in ~5 km; boat access required)

trailheads.name: Lake Lovely Water Trailhead, west bank of Squamish River (boat/canoe drop)

routes.permits: No park permit or camping fee (~15 first-come tent pads at the lake) but you must arrange the Squamish River crossing (jet-boat ~$60 CAD/person, or helicopter); east-bank access crosses Squamish Nation land where permission should be sought. The 16-bunk ACC Tantalus Hut rents whole-hut through ACC Vancouver.
routes.highlights: A fjord-like alpine lake ringed by the glaciered Tantalus Range summits, with near-guaranteed solitude for the corridor.
routes.hazards: Committing access (missed boat pickups strand you), a relentlessly steep slippery trail, brutal July mosquitoes.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); regional wildfire smoke possible.

routes.name: Athelney Pass via Salal Creek
routes.difficulty: hard - an unmaintained route, not a trail

trailheads.name: Salal Creek route start, Upper Lillooet FSR past Garibaldi Pumice mine

routes.permits: No permits, fees or reservations - remote crown land north of Pemberton; only constraints are active mine/logging traffic on the Upper Lillooet FSR and a high-clearance vehicle. Route is largely unmarked and not drawn in full on this map.
routes.highlights: A glacier-ringed 1,830 m pass among Ochre Mountain, Salal Peak and the Icemaker, with volcanic pumice landscapes and near-total solitude.
routes.hazards: Grizzly country with multiple glacial creek crossings best at low water (mid-late August), loose unstable rock, no marked trail or cell coverage.
routes.status_2026: No known closures on the Upper Lillooet FSR (early Aug 2026); the Bonanza Creek fire burns across the divide to the northeast - expect smoke and verify FSR status.

routes.name: McGillivray Pass (Anderson Lake to Bralorne historic route)

trailheads.name: Standard Creek access via Cadwallader Creek road from Bralorne
McGillivray townsite side, Anderson Lake (High Line Rd)

routes.permits: No permits or fees - a historic gold-rush pack route on crown land; the cabins near the 1,867 m pass are private (McGillivray Pass Lodge), so plan to tent in the subalpine meadows.
routes.highlights: A wildflower-carpeted high valley linking the Bendor and Cadwallader Ranges, walked by miners between Bralorne's gold mines and the railway.
routes.hazards: Remote valley with faded tread and deadfall, significant grizzly activity, confusing old mine roads - GPS and self-sufficiency essential.
routes.status_2026: CAUTION: the Bonanza Creek fire (~17,800 ha as of Aug 6, 2026) burns north of Gold Bridge with an evacuation ORDER for the South Chilcotins and alerts around Gold Bridge - Bralorne-side access is unreliable right now; check SLRD. Anderson Lake side unaffected so far.

routes.name: Blowdown Pass, Blowdown Lake and Gott Peak
routes.difficulty: moderate (old mining road to the pass)

trailheads.name: Blowdown FSR parking at ~1,650 m (4WD spur off Hwy 99 east of Duffey Lake)

routes.permits: No permits, fees or reservations - informal free camping at Blowdown Lake below the pass (the pass itself is the Stein Valley park boundary); a capable 4WD determines how much of the road you walk.
routes.highlights: Larch-fringed lake camp at 2,000 m with an easy sunrise walk up 2,481 m Gott Peak and ridgelines overlooking the headwaters of the Stein.
routes.hazards: Rough, brushy spur road, fully exposed alpine weather, grizzly presence in the Cottonwood/Blowdown drainages.
routes.status_2026: No known closures (early Aug 2026); smoke likely at times from the Twin Two Creek and Cariboo fires.
